correctness.rationale: For the expressly named Becker–Baraviera/Reyes shift, Reyes v1 confirms the full transition: after a 1 the next symbol is 1 at or below the threshold and 0 above it (after a 0 either is allowed). The frozen description should spell out the above-threshold branch; treating it as a free choice would instead allow any finite word after a sufficiently long prefix of ones, giving the full shift after closure. For the named system Reyes's Theorems C–D give the entropy and uniqueness, with equality to the coded shift at k=1 and invariant-measure support on the coded subsystem for k≥2. Junction sampling gives the regenerative law q_m=2^(−m), for which entropy per codeword is 2 log 2 and mean length is 2(k+1); the decoded stationary suspension attains the required entropy. The block covering a typical time is size-biased, not part of the junction iid assertion. The iid tail is 2^(−r). A deterministic index sandwich around N/[2(k+1)] via the renewal strong law, without a spurious independence assumption between count and lengths, gives the stated o(1) law because N2^(−r_N) stays bounded. Taking floors away from the lattice phase boundaries gives the subsequential formula. Dyadic tail estimates and monotonic interpolation give the almost-sure logarithmic block maximum. The within-block potential goes from 0 to −km and back, so its difference at times 0 and n is S_n. The initial potential has all stationary moments; for the maximum the completed and all intersecting block maxima sandwich the pathwise depth and have the same asymptotic order and coefficient. This does not assert that the terminal partial block's own length is o(log N). Uniform second moments give zero variance per time.
residual_risks: Passing correctness is for the cited shift with the deterministic after-1 transition, not a weaker prefix rule, an arbitrary invariant measure, or an iff characterization of parameters for entropy equality. The frozen finite rational diagnostics do not prove the stochastic limits and were not replayed.
